title: Meta
summary: Problems whose patterns are commonly reported in Meta coding interviews, from Easy to Hard. Approximate and hand curated, not an official or verified question list.
lesson:
About this list
- Each problem practices a pattern that candidates commonly describe from Meta technical interviews: two-pointer string and palindrome checks, prefix sums, binary trees and lowest common ancestors, BFS/DFS graph traversal, sliding windows, intervals, heaps/quickselect, and clean in-place array manipulation.
- Problems are grouped Easy, Medium, and Hard so you can build speed and accuracy on core patterns before tackling multi-constraint windows, codecs, and shortest-path searches.
- The selection is approximate. Interviewers select their own prompts and follow-ups across teams, so treat this track as pattern practice rather than a prediction of what you will be asked.

What to expect
- Candidates often report fast-paced 45-minute coding rounds with two medium-scale problems where bug-free implementation and clear dry-running matter.
- Follow-ups frequently ask to reduce extra space (for example O(1) space two-pointer scans), handle streaming or skewed inputs, or adapt a tree/graph traversal for an extra constraint.
- Interviewers commonly expect you to walk through a concrete example line by line and catch off-by-one or null/empty edge cases before relying on execution.

How to prepare
- Practice stating the exact time and space complexity upfront and verifying whether an O(n) or O(n log k) approach exists before writing code.
- Drill tree recursion vs. iterative BFS/DFS and two-pointer invariants until you can code them cleanly without hesitating on boundary conditions.
- After passing, dry-run your code on empty inputs, single-element inputs, ties, and worst-case shapes.
